purpose: Resolve US search/counterstrike after the Japanese dawn raid reveals a return bearing, while preserving the Japanese planned westward egress and applying sea-going rather than fixed-base Japanese fighter-direction quality.

timeline.event: US groups recover raid survivors, detach immediate aid toward Cabot, and launch broad western searches along the Japanese raid return bearing. TG58.1/58.3 carry most of the search/counterstrike burden while TG58.2 deals with damage and recovery.
A US carrier scout obtains a visual on the retiring Japanese carrier force, identifying at least three fleet carriers with fast heavy escorts. Report is fresh enough for a long-range counterstrike.
TG58.1 and TG58.3 launch the principal counterstrike; TG58.2 contributes only a limited component because Cabot is mission-killed and Intrepid deck operations are interrupted.
Japanese shipboard radar/passive warning and visual pickets provide useful but non-US-grade warning. Layered CAP meets the strike, with Kinsei fighters concentrated in high-cover/fast-intercept duty.
US bombers penetrate portions of the CAP and heavy AA. The Japanese formation maintains westward withdrawal rather than turning back for a second offensive cycle.

US_counterstrike.mission: carrier attack with strong F6F escort; no claim that all launch aircraft reach target

Japanese_defense.note: Sea-going carrier CAP gets carrier-process maturation and improved warning but not the A-grade fixed-base radar/plot bonus.

centered_damage.Hiryu: One bomb hit plus a damaging near miss centered on aft flight-deck/hangar region. Flight operations cease for the rest of 3 Feb; propulsion and withdrawal speed remain adequate. Surviving airborne aircraft recover preferentially on Shokaku/Zuikaku or are diverted as fuel permits.
centered_damage.Shokaku: Near-miss/splinter/light topside damage only centered; deck remains operational.
centered_damage.screen: Minor splinter/near-miss damage on one or two escorts; no named escort loss centered.

carrier_battle_cumulative_3Feb.Japan_ship_state: Shokaku/Zuikaku operational; Hiryu mission-limited by flight-deck damage but mobile. No Japanese carrier sunk centered.
carrier_battle_cumulative_3Feb.US_ship_state: Cabot campaign-out from fast-carrier operations pending repair; Intrepid temporarily disrupted but not campaign-out; remaining fast decks operational.

decision: Both sides terminate the carrier exchange after one main offensive cycle each. Japan withdraws west rather than trading its remaining carrier cadre into the still larger US deck pool; US does not launch a second same-day deep counterstrike without another fresh fix.
downstream: Cabot repair duration and Hiryu repair duration require separate damage/yard audit before Truk/next-carrier-operation wallets are used.
